definitions.explanation: The formal ritual of exchanging business cards when meeting someone in a professional setting. A key part of Japanese business etiquette.

examples.japanese: まず{名刺交換|めいしこうかん}をしましょう。
{会議|かいぎ}の{前|まえ}に{名刺交換|めいしこうかん}を{済|す}ませた。
examples.english: We finished exchanging business cards before the meeting.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{名刺交換|めいしこうかん}のマナーがとても{大切|たいせつ}にされている。
examples.english: In Japan, the etiquette of exchanging business cards is considered very important.

notes:
A compound of {名刺|めいし} (business card) + {交換|こうかん} (exchange). In Japanese business culture, this ritual follows specific rules of etiquette.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名刺交換|めいしこうかん}をする: to exchange business cards
- {名刺交換|めいしこうかん}を{済|す}ませる: to finish exchanging cards
- {名刺交換|めいしこうかん}のマナー: business card exchange etiquette

CULTURAL NOTE:
When exchanging business cards in Japan, one should present the card with both hands, with the text facing the recipient. Received cards should be treated respectfully — never written on, bent, or placed carelessly. During a meeting, received cards are typically lined up on the table in front of you as a reference.
